source_excerpts.text:
4. Observable acceptance and restoration

The controller receives observations, not the injected fault label:

Individual head orientations.
Four disc travels.
Four seating gaps.
Crossbolt bearing overlap.
Proof motion and residual set.
Separation force.
Data validity and calibration identity.

Required verified uncertainties are approximately ±1.5° for head angle, ±10 µm for local travel/gap, ±15 µm for total motion, ±0.03° for rotation and ±2 N for separation force. These are calibration requirements, not invented instrument achievements.

The proposed gate requires, among other conditions:

Gap upper uncertainty bound ≤40 µm.
Disc-travel interval inside 150–225 µm.
Actual crossbolt overlap ≥3 mm.
Residual deformation upper bound ≤30 µm.
Reference displacement and rotation inside their declared limits.
Separation force upper bound ≤20 N.

The model deliberately contains a latent-crack example with identical observations. The gate accepts it. That is an admitted observability limit: finite sensing cannot establish the absence of every future failure mechanism.

title: Use actual observations and retain the indistinguishability limit
